req.title: Login required for update
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they attempt GET /<id>/update.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-013 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users attempting GET /<id>/update are redirected to /auth/login. Three test cases are designed: (1) positive — an authenticated user can access the update page without redirect; (2) negative — an anonymous user gets a 302 redirect to /auth/login; (3) boundary — the redirect Location header is exactly '/auth/login' (not a prefix, not a superset). Each test uses exact-value assertions to kill constant-mutation, comparison-flip, and boolean-negation mutants. The pre-loaded database has post id=1 authored by user id=5 (James/river) and post id=2 authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone).

trace: R-FLASKR-013: anonymous GET /<id>/update must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_get_update_redirects_to_login()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_authenticated_user_get_update_succeeds():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():

    client = app.test_client()

tests.name: test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exact_login_path
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is pre-loaded with seed data (post id=1 exists)
No session cookie is present (anonymous client)
actions: Send GET /1/update with no authentication cookie
Inspect the exact string value of the Location header
Verify the Location header is not a superset or prefix of the expected path
expected: Location header equals '/auth/login' exactly — not '/auth/login/' or '/auth/login?next=...' or any other variant
Status code is exactly 302 — not 301, not 303, not 307
trace: R-FLASKR-013: redirect must target exactly /auth/login; boundary test catches constant mutations in url_for('auth.login') resolution and status-code off-by-one mutations
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exact_login_path():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.status_code != 301
    assert r.status_code != 303
    assert location == '/auth/login'
    assert location != '/auth/login/'
    assert not location.startswith('/auth/login?')

test_anonymous_redirect_location_is_exact_login_path()

tests.name: test_state_transition_logout_then_get_update_redirects
preconditions: Application is initialised with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
Database is pre-loaded with seed data (post id=2 authored by Rahul exists)
User Rahul logs in, then logs out, transitioning back to anonymous state
actions: Send GET /2/update with the now-anonymous session
expected: Location header after logout is exactly '/auth/login'
trace: R-FLASKR-013: state transition from authenticated -> anonymous must restore redirect behaviour; catches mutations that skip session clearing in logout
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_state_transition_logout_then_get_update_redirects():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    authed_r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert authed_r.status_code == 200
    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/2/update')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_state_transition_logout_then_get_update_redirects()
